draft.title: Comparing costs of owning and renting
card: To compare buying with renting, add up every cost over the same period of time. The price tag alone is not enough.
the purchase price, plus running costs such as loan interest, insurance and repairs. Some of the money may come back if the item is sold.
regular rent payments, plus any extra costs the rental has. Nothing comes back at the end, because the owner keeps the item.

Example: a car costs $12 000 to buy. Running it costs $2000 a year, and after 3 years it sells for $7000. Cost of owning = 12 000 + 3 × 2000 − 7000 = $11 000. Renting costs $300 a month, so 36 × 300 = $10 800, with running costs included.
draft.remember: Compare total costs over the same time, and take off any money you get back.

a.q: Using the card's method, a van costs $20 000 to buy, $1500 a year to run, and sells for $12 000 after 4 years. What is the total cost of owning it for 4 years?
a.why: Total cost = 20 000 + 4 × 1500 − 12 000 = 20 000 + 6000 − 12 000 = $14 000. The $8000 answer is the price less the resale value only, which leaves out the running costs.
a.clue: Add the price and 4 years of running costs, then take off the sale money.

b.q: Tariq can buy a scooter for $5000, which costs $400 a year to run and sells for $2000 after 3 years. Or he can rent one for $190 a month, with running costs included. Which is cheaper over 3 years, and by how much?
b.why: Owning costs 5000 + 3 × 400 − 2000 = $4200. Renting costs 36 × 190 = $6840. Owning is cheaper by 6840 − 4200 = $2640. Check against the options: none matches, so recompute 36 × 190 = 6840 and 6840 − 4200 = 2640.
b.clue: Find both totals over 36 months, then subtract.
